channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Twenty-Eight Social Facilities Commissioned in Tokmok Over Five Years
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov reviewed the socio-economic development results for Tokmok (2021-2026). During this period, 28 social facilities were commissioned, including institutions for higher education, schools, kindergartens, sports facilities, parks, and a swimming pool. New administrative and public service buildings were also put into use.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Expand Investment Cooperation and Privatization Ties
item.description: Uzbekistan's Director of State Assets Management met with the Chairman of the Turkish-Uzbek Business Council to discuss attracting Turkish investors to privatization processes. A memorandum was signed to inform Turkish companies about privatization, exchange investment proposals, and establish systematic interaction. A special session for investors is planned for December.

item.title: Deputy Head of Afghanistan's National Unity Government Returns from Iran
item.description: Engineer Mohammad Khan Rahmani, deputy head of Afghanistan's National Unity Government executive office, has returned to the country from Iran, according to the Taliban's 'Commission for Contact with Afghan Personalities'. Rahmani expressed happiness upon his return and thanked the commission.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Caution on High-Interest Loans After Citizen Loses Home
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov advised citizens to carefully consider loan terms and interest rates after a resident lost their home due to defaulting on a high-interest mortgage. The citizen took a loan at 31% annual interest, but could not repay it, leading to the loss of their property valued at nearly $100,000.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Capitalize on US-China Competition for Resources
item.description: Several countries, including one in Central Asia, are benefiting from the strategic competition between the US and China for critical resources and metals. Both superpowers are investing billions in mining, allowing these nations to attract capital from both sides simultaneously. This dynamic presents significant economic opportunities.

item.title: Kyrgyz Farmers Urge President to Increase Crop Purchase Prices
item.description: Kyrgyz farmers are facing difficulties due to stagnant prices for agricultural products like sugar beet and corn, while fertilizer and fuel costs rise. They appealed to President Sadyr Japarov to raise purchase prices, noting losses since 2023. The Agriculture Minister stated efforts are underway to increase sugar beet prices and reduce fertilizer costs.

item.title: Tokmok Sees Growth: 11 Large and 201 Small Businesses Opened in Five Years
item.description: Tokmok city has experienced a revitalization of its industrial sector. Over the past five years, 11 large enterprises were launched, creating 423 jobs. Additionally, 201 small and medium-sized businesses opened, providing 2,117 jobs. New facilities include a cheese producer, tire recycling plant, and construction material factories.

item.title: Uzbekistan Allocates 49 Trillion Som to Healthcare, Life Expectancy Reaches 75.4 Years
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated medical workers as Uzbekistan's annual healthcare funding reached 49 trillion som. He noted the creation of medical records for over 38 million citizens via the DMED system, contributing to an increased average life expectancy of 75.4 years.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches International Initiative at UNESCO for Cultural Heritage Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched an international initiative at UNESCO to enhance the protection of cultural heritage amidst globalization and climate change. Approved by the UNESCO Executive Board, the initiative aims to safeguard tangible and intangible heritage, conduct risk assessments, and strengthen international cooperation.

item.title: Over 3200 Tashkent Residents Dispute Housing Valuation Results as Overstated
item.description: More than 3,200 Tashkent property owners have reported that the results of the first mass housing valuation were overstated. Public discussions on the valuation results are extended until December 4, allowing owners to challenge or comment on the assessed values.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Garden Catering Trade Executives Sentenced to Prison for Mass Food Poisoning
item.description: In Uzbekistan's Fergana region, the head and technologist of Garden Catering Trade have been sentenced to real prison terms for the mass poisoning of 105 children in kindergartens. A cassation court revised the initial sentences of restricted freedom, imposing four years for the head and three years and six months for the technologist.

item.title: US Central Command Establishes Task Force to Disrupt Iran's Transit Routes
item.description: US Central Command (CENTCOM) has established a special task force named 'Iron Gate' to prevent Iran from using land routes for advanced weapons and other items. The task force, based in Florida, will coordinate with other US agencies to block the movement of advanced weapon systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned goods, and illicit financial flows through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.

item.title: 67 Social Facilities Commissioned in Yessyk-Ata District Over Last Five Years
item.description: In the last five years, 67 social facilities have been commissioned in the Yessyk-Ata district. This includes 7 schools, 9 paramedic-obstetric points, 30 mini-football fields, 4 sports halls, 1 kindergarten, 2 family doctor groups, 12 service houses, and 2 water supply facilities. The information was announced during President Sadyr Japarov's review of the district's socio-economic development.

item.title: Eight Major Industrial Enterprises Opened in Yessyk-Ata District in Nine Months
item.description: Eight major industrial enterprises were opened in the Yessyk-Ata district in the first nine months of the year. Four more large enterprises are planned to be commissioned by the end of the year, and 15 industrial facilities are scheduled for launch in 2027. This information was announced during President Sadyr Japarov's review of the district's socio-economic development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Ban on Export of Gasoline and Diesel Fuel for Six Months
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended its ban on the export of gasoline, diesel fuel, and certain other petroleum products by road transport for another six months. The restrictions, effective from November 22, 2026, to May 22, 2027, apply to exports to Eurasian Economic Union member states as well.

item.title: Canada Rejects Afghan Teenager's Study Permit Despite Full Scholarship
item.description: Canadian immigration authorities have denied a study permit to an 18-year-old Afghan girl who had received a full scholarship to attend a British Columbia boarding school. The department cited concerns she would not return to Afghanistan and lacked sufficient funds, despite the scholarship covering all expenses.

item.title: Uzbek President Congratulates Healthcare Workers on Professional Holiday, Highlights Reforms
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Uzbekistan's medical and pharmaceutical workers on their professional holiday, emphasizing reforms in the healthcare sector, increased funding, and improved life expectancy. He noted a sevenfold increase in healthcare financing, reaching 49 trillion soms by 2026, and the digitalization of medical services.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Provide Housing to Residents Affected by Border Conflict
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will allocate 170 houses, transferred from Tajikistan through land exchange, to residents of the Batken region. These homes are intended for citizens who lost their housing during the border conflicts in 2021-2022.

item.title: Prosecutor's Office Overturns Illegal Market Owner Requirements in Abay Region
item.description: The prosecutor's office in the Makanchy district of Abay Region has overturned an illegal requirement imposed on market owners. The district administration had mandated that market owners provide land for temporary trading objects free of charge, violating entrepreneurs' rights. The official responsible for the regulation has been fined.

item.title: West Kazakhstan Governor Classifies Rally Refusal Statistics as Confidential
item.description: The governor of West Kazakhstan region has classified statistics on refusals for peaceful rallies as confidential. The Kazakhstan International Bureau for Human Rights and Rule of Law reported this. Since May 2020, Kazakhstan has amended its laws on peaceful assemblies, requiring only prior notification instead of permits.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Security Chief Reports Rise in Extremist Online Content
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Security Service identified over 49,000 extremist and terrorist online resources in early 2026, a 14% increase from the previous year. The head of the service stated that terrorist groups increasingly use digital technologies for propaganda and operations. Uzbekistan ranks low on the Global Terrorism Index.

item.title: Astana Hosts Traditional 'Sogym-FEST' Meat Fair with Competitive Prices
item.description: Astana has launched its traditional 'Sogym-FEST' meat fair, offering products from various regions of Kazakhstan at competitive prices. Beef is sold at 3,300 tenge per kilogram, horse meat at 3,500 tenge, and lamb at 3,700 tenge. The fair aims to sell over 1,000 tons of meat by the end of the season.

item.title: Afghan Women Cricketers Urge Foreign Players to Boycott Afghanistan Premier League
item.description: Afghan refugee women cricketers are calling on foreign players to boycott the upcoming Afghanistan Premier League, scheduled to be held in the UAE. They argue that foreign participation would legitimize the current situation where women are banned from sports in Afghanistan since the Taliban's return to power in 2021.

item.title: Italian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister's personal data leaked online
item.description: Pro-Russian hackers have published the personal data of Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Antonio Tajani. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called the incident a serious threat. Tajani linked the cyberattack to Italy's support for Ukraine and efforts to strengthen digital security.

item.title: Uzbekistan prioritizes skills and professional potential for international labor market
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing conditions for citizens seeking employment abroad, focusing on professional qualifications and international labor market demands. The government emphasizes the need for sought-after specialties, skills, language proficiency, and legal guarantees for successful overseas employment. This was a key discussion point at a recent meeting chaired by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Russian Billionaire Alexander Mashrabov Obtains Kazakh Citizenship
item.description: Alexander Mashrabov, co-founder of the AI startup Higgsfield, has been granted Kazakh citizenship. The decree was signed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev on October 30. Mashrabov, who resides in the US, previously renounced his Russian citizenship.

item.title: Man Arrested in Almaty for Selling Fake Documents to Foreigners
item.description: Police in Almaty have arrested a 32-year-old man for producing and selling counterfeit documents to foreign nationals. The suspect used real Kazakh identification numbers but altered photos and personal data. These fake documents allowed clients to register for services like delivery and ride-sharing, concealing their identities. Authorities seized computer equipment and a mobile phone used in the forgery.

item.title: UN Chief Stresses Upholding Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity Without Double Standards
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres emphasized the need to uphold respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of all countries, without double standards. He stated that the UN Charter has been instrumental in preventing a third world war over the past 80 years, establishing a common rule of law for all nations.

item.title: Shymkent's Ordabasy Football Club Achieves Historic Double by Winning Kazakhstan Cup
item.description: Shymkent's Ordabasy football club has won the Kazakhstan Cup, defeating Kaisar 4-1 in the final. This victory, following their earlier Kazakhstan Premier League title, secures a historic 'golden double' for the club. Ordabasy is the first team since Astana in 2016 to achieve this feat.

item.title: Gaza Health Ministry Reports Over 74,000 Deaths from Israeli Attacks Since October 2023
item.description: Gaza's Health Ministry announced that the death toll from Israeli attacks since October 2023 has reached 74,640. Over the past 48 hours, 10 people were killed, including two recovered from rubble and two who died from injuries. The ministry also stated 1,610 deaths occurred since the October 2025 ceasefire.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Public Not to Praise Government or Him
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan has asked citizens not to praise the government or himself. This statement encourages a focus on constructive criticism and accountability rather than public adulation. The president's request aims to foster a more objective evaluation of governance.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Presidents Inaugurate New Tajik Embassy in Astana
item.description: Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Emomali Rahmon attended the grand opening of the new Tajik Embassy in Astana. They cut the ceremonial ribbon, and the Presidential Orchestra performed the national anthems of both countries. The leaders also viewed a presentation about the embassy and planted saplings on the grounds.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Complete Ban on Energy Drink Production and Import
item.description: The Kyrgyz government will review a potential ban on energy drink production and import within a month, following a presidential directive. President Sadyr Japarov cited health risks associated with increased consumption. The move could impact budget revenues by approximately 1.5 billion soms.

item.title: Afghanistan U19 Cricket Team Defeats Malaysia by Ten Wickets
item.description: Afghanistan's U19 cricket team secured a dominant ten-wicket victory against Malaysia in their second Asia Cup match. Malaysia was bowled out for just 42 runs, setting a low target that Afghanistan chased down without losing any wickets in the third over.

item.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Held Talks with 12 Countries on Regional Developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced he held discussions with the foreign ministers of 12 nations regarding regional developments over the past 48 hours. He outlined Iran's stance and emphasized respecting sovereignty and preventing insecurity. Discussions also focused on regional security mechanisms without external powers' involvement.

item.title: Taliban Intelligence Confirms Arrest of Former Afghan Police Commander
item.description: Taliban intelligence media has confirmed the arrest of Allahdad Fadaei, a former Afghan police commander. The outlet claims Fadaei worked for the 'United Afghanistan Front' led by Sami Sadat, a claim the front denies, calling the audio messages 'fake and AI-generated'.

item.title: Uzbekistan Energy Ministry Warns of Possible CNG Station Restrictions Due to Cold Snap
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy has warned of potential temporary restrictions on compressed natural gas (CNG) stations from November 9-11 due to a cold snap and predicted frosts. Gas supply will prioritize residential areas, schools, kindergartens, and hospitals. This is a recurring issue during colder months, affecting many drivers who rely on CNG.

item.title: Tashkent Begins Heating Season on November 9
item.description: The heating season in Tashkent will commence on Monday, November 9. The city administration announced a phased connection, prioritizing social facilities such as schools, kindergartens, and hospitals before supplying residential buildings. Payment for heating services will be charged from the day of connection.

item.title: Kabul University Reopens Amidst Taliban Rule and Women's Protests
item.description: Kabul University reopened on September 6, 2022, months after the Taliban takeover. Women's protests demanding "Bread, Work and Freedom" continued across the city, challenging Taliban rule despite facing repression. Their resistance is highlighted as a significant historical event.

item.title: US Offers Up to $20 Million Reward for Information on Iran's Nuclear Program
item.description: The U.S. Department of State is offering up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program through its "Rewards for Justice" program. The announcement seeks details on facilities, equipment, personnel, and technical aspects. This comes amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions between the US and Iran.
